Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Underwriting Officer; Emily Rivera, Chief Investment Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by our rock-solid capital position and statutory surplus growth, robust investment income yields amid stabilizing rates, favorable loss ratio trends through better claims management, strategic capital deployment into high-return opportunities, refined actuarial assumptions boosting reserves, and an outstanding combined ratio across segments. We are particularly excited about the initial success of our EMBARK digital platform for SMB casualty coverage and its rapid scaling toward $2 billion in premiums by 2025.

Maria, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Maria Lopez: Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $1.4 billion, or $4.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included underwriting profitability from improved loss picks, earned premium expansion, steady expense leverage, and resilient investment returns. Our combined ratio was 92.5%. Investment income for the quarter was $2.0 billion, reflecting strong performance in our fixed income and alternatives segments. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with consolidated statutory surplus at $15.8 billion.

Let me walk you through our capital position and statutory surplus levels in more detail. Our balance sheet remains exceptionally strong, well-positioned to handle elevated catastrophe activity from hurricane season and the evolving cyber risk environment while pursuing growth. As of September 30th, our consolidated statutory surplus reached $15.8 billion, up 11% year-over-year and 4% from Q2. This was fueled by about $1.2 billion in operating earnings retention from underwriting gains and investment income, plus favorable realized gains on fixed income as Fed rates stabilized. In our Property & Casualty segment, surplus hit $12.1 billion, a 13% YoY rise, while Life & Health added $3.7 billion, up 5%, thanks to stable long-tail reserves.

Our Risk-Based Capital ratios highlight this: consolidated at 512%, far exceeding the NAIC's 200% action level and our 450% internal target. P&C stood at 548% with proactive reinsurance, Group Life at 420% from better lapse rates in term products, and Health at 465% via Medicare Advantage improvements. These outpace peers like Chubb at 480% and Allstate at 460%, reflecting our conservative reserving and asset-liability matching. Over the past year, surplus has grown at a 10% CAGR since Q4 2022, beating the industry's 7% per AM Best, even with $450 million in YTD pre-tax cat losses from wildfires and storms.

Regionally, U.S. operations, 65% of surplus, anchor us, with Southeast exposure trimmed to 12% of net writings through excess-of-loss towers at $200 million xs $50 million, backed by $800 million in cat reserves. Europe surplus grew 15% to $2.4 billion on commercial D&O demand under Solvency II, exceeding 180% SCR. Asia-Pacific, 18% of the portfolio, expanded to $1.9 billion with 22% premium growth in cyber and parametric lines, supported by a 25% quota share with Munich Re on our $1.5 billion book.

We've optimized capital through a $500 million cat bond issuance—our third via Apex Re Ltd.—transferring U.S. hurricane and quake peak risks, cutting RBC volatility by 25 bps. Plus $300 million in ILWs collateralized at 110%. Our portfolio yield climbed to 4.8% from 4.2%, with 92% NAIC 1-2 quality and 5.2-year duration matching liabilities. Swaps on 40% of floating munis protected against Q3's 50 bps rate dip.

This positions us to deploy $1.5 billion this year: $600 million in buybacks at $85 average, $400 million in supplemental dividends yielding 2.8%, and $500 million into EMBARK. Our ORSA testing covers cyber and climate risks, keeping us ahead of NAIC standards. We see 8-10% surplus growth in 2025 at normalized cats and 4.5% yields, with RBC stable in a 100-year hurricane.

Shifting to investment income yield, which hit 4.35% annualized this quarter on $185 billion average invested assets. That's 25 bps above last year's Q3 and 10 bps better sequentially, with YTD at 4.28%, topping our 4.0-4.2% guide and eyeing over 4.3% full-year. Calculated as net investment income post-expenses over average assets, it shows our ALM strength preserving AA- ratings in this rate regime.

Fixed maturities, 72% of the book, yielded 4.65%, led by IG corporates at 5.12% with spreads at 105 bps over Treasuries, RMBS at 5.45% on agency pools, and munis at 4.8% tax-equivalent from infrastructure. Equities, 12%, added 3.2% via dividend aristocrats like P&G and JPM. Alternatives, now 16%, shone at 6.75% from direct lending at 8.2%, AA CLOs at 7.1%, and core-plus RE at 6.5%, rotating via Ares and Blackstone.

The Fed's hikes lag into new money at 5.8%, 150 bps over 2021 lows, shortening book yield lag with $22 billion annual maturities and duration at 6.2 years versus 8.1-year liabilities. Swaps locked $1.2 billion at 4.9% synthetics, CDS managed BBB spreads, ESG bonds at 28% of new commitments yielded 4.9%, and Aladdin optimized cash to 5.3% MMFs.

U.S. (65%) exceeded 4.6% on Treasuries and credit supply; Europe (20%) at 3.9% improved via UK gilts and BBBs; Asia-Pacific (15%) at 4.2% with hedges preserving yields. We're committing $5 billion to private assets at 7-9%, supporting VA options income of $450 million YTD. A steepening curve adds 20-30 bps; stress tests handle 200 bps spreads.

This contributed 28% to pre-tax operating income, backing 14-16% ROE.

On loss ratio trends and drivers, our consolidated figure was 63.2%, down 120 bps YoY from 64.4% and 50 bps from Q2, with ex-CAT at 59.1%, up 40 bps YoY on 8.7% earned premium growth to $3.2 billion. YTD at 64.8% versus 66.1%, ex-CAT 60.3%, ahead of Progressive's 65.8%, Allstate's 68.2%, Travelers' 62.5%.

Frequency flat QoQ at 102% of 2019 baseline but up 3% YoY in auto from miles driven and distractions; severity up 7.2% YoY to $18,400 per claim from repair (15% labor hike), medical, and parts inflation (12%).

Personal Auto (42% EP): 68.5%, ex-CAT 64.2%; frequency +4.5% to 1.12, severity +9% to $12,200; Snapshot telematics cut safe driver frequency 18%, aiding 150 bps.

Homeowners (28%): 55.4%, ex-CAT 48.7%; stable frequency, +6.8% severity to $28,500; Florida wind down 12%.

Commercial (22%): 58.9%, ex-CAT 54.1%; WC frequency +2%, GL severity +8.5% to $42,700 from social inflation.

Specialty (8%): 52.3%, ex-CAT 49.8%; cyber frequency x2 but AI triage capped severity at $1.2M.

U.S. (82%) at 64.1%; Europe (12%) 59.8%; Asia-Pac (6%) 56.2%.

Headwinds: med trends 5.8%, repairs 11%; tailwinds: used cars down 4%. ClaimsNext AI cut cycle 22%, NLP subrogation +$45M; Risk360 improved selection 12%. 6.5% personal rates, 92% reinsurance retention. Guide ex-CAT 59.5-60.5% full-year, mid-50s by 2027.

Turning to combined ratio analysis, overall 92.5%, 270 bps better YoY from 95.2%, 40 bps from Q2's 92.9%; full-year guide 93-94% versus 95-97% initial. Ex-CAT 87.8%. Loss 65.2% from auto PD moderation, large losses -5%; expense 27.3% with 28.5% variable leverage via UnityAI. PYD +120 bps.

Personal Lines (46%, $2.8B EP): 90.1%, ex-cat 86.5%; auto 91.2%, homeowners 88.7%.

Commercial (32%, $1.9B): 94.3%, best in 5 years; WC 92.5%, GL offset inflation.

Specialty (18%, $1.1B): 88.7%; cyber 86.2%, D&O 89.4%.

U.S. 92.0%; Europe 90.8%; Asia-Pac 96.5%.

Trends: auto frequency -7%, severity +3.2%, pricing +9.5%; cats $320M or 5.4 pts. UnityAI automated 40% underwriting, gen AI cut leakage 8%, parametrics up 25%.

Portfolio shift to specialty (28%), exiting CA risk. Mid-90s sustain 12-14% ROE.

Regarding changes in actuarial assumptions, we had a net $285 million pre-tax favorable impact, or 12 cents EPS. Life & Annuity ($18.7B AV, 45%): $210M release from mortality 2-3% better post-COVID/SOA, FIA lapses -15 bps to 4.2%, rates to 4.25%. U.S. 70%, Europe milder longevity, Asia lower morbidity.

P&C ($12.4B prem): $95M unfavorable from BF ULR +1.8 pts to 62.5% on inflation, cat loading +5%; PYD $142M offset. U.S. storms drove 60%.

Group Health (15%, $4.2B): $20M favorable on disability -1.2%, but pharmacy +1.7 pts to 11.5% from GLP-1s.

AAS process with Deloitte review; ML stochastic reserving cut times 40%. Low volatility ahead.

Finally, capital deployment plans: $12.4B deployable excess, up 8% QoQ on 92.4% ex-CAT P&C. Pillars: returns (55%, $1.8B)—dividend +10% to $0.65 (2.8% yield), $1.2B buybacks at $148 ($3.2B left); M&A (30%, $2.1B)—$1.4B Midwest E&S ($850M GWP, 15¢ EPS acc), $700M EuroParametric for parametrics ($150M GWP run-rate); organic (40%, $1.3B)—Apex CyberShield Pro ($220M GWP, 55% LR), Apex Vitality 2.0 wearables, InsureTech Forge cloud migration (200 bps expense cut).

U.S. P&C growth, Asia 18% CAGR, Europe motor. Tilt to specialty ROE>20%, alts 15%. $6-8B for 2025, robust pipeline.

David Chen: Thank you, Maria. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial lines segment. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including our GLIDE pricing algorithm that dynamically adjusts for frequency in auto and habitational exposures, alongside AI triage in claims and telematics penetration.

Emily Rivera: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed maturities, IG corporates, RMBS, alternatives like direct lending and CLOs, with tactical rotations and hedges ensuring stability.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Harlan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Harlan: Good morning. Can you provide more color on your capital deployment plans, particularly M&A and new products?

Alex Thompson: Good morning, Mike. Absolutely. As Maria detailed, we're deploying opportunistically with a focus on high-ROE areas. The Midwest Specialty and EuroParametric deals add E&S scale and parametric innovation, accretive immediately, while organic launches like CyberShield and Vitality leverage tech for cyber growth and health persistency. This balances returns—dividends and buybacks—with growth, targeting mid-teens ROE.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity on your business?

Maria Lopez: Good morning, Lisa. Cats were $320 million pre-tax or 5.4 points this quarter, managed well below budget via our robust towers—$1.2 billion aggregate, ILWs, cat bonds. This kept ex-CAT combined at 87.8%, and reinsurance recoveries covered most, with strikes raised and quota shares in place. We're positioned for rebuild cycles with reserves ring-fenced.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly: What is the expected impact of upcoming cyber regulatory changes on your underwriting strategy?

David Chen: Good morning, Tom. New regs like expanded SEC disclosure rules will drive demand for our cyber products, where we're ahead with AI scoring and CrowdStrike integration. We'll adjust attachments and rates up 12%, maintaining sub-60% loss ratios via real-time intel and parametric options. No major disruption—our specialty mix gives flexibility.

Operator: Our next question comes from Karen Weiss with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Karen Weiss: Thanks. On actuarial assumptions, how sensitive are reserves to further rate changes?

Maria Lopez: Karen, good question. The $285 million favorability was from mortality, lapses, and rates to 4.25%, stress-tested via ESG models. A 50 bps Fed cut would add modest volatility, offset by swaps; we're conservative with 95% confidence in RBC. Stability expected barring longevity shifts.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That concludes today's questions.

Alex Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
